name: Otsu on grayscale
why: Baseline. Eggs are bright, so the simplest global threshold shows how far brightness alone goes.

name: Keep largest component
why: T01 labels every bright pixel; most images hold one main object.

name: Median blur and open/close
why: Speckle and texture fragment the mask and join it to the background.

name: LAB lightness channel
why: Perceptual lightness may separate eggs better than gray.

name: Whiteness channel (L minus chroma)
why: Hands, pink bowls and fabrics are bright but coloured; shells are not.

name: Adaptive threshold
why: Uneven lighting defeats one global level; a local threshold might not.

name: Select by ellipse fit, not size
why: The largest bright region is often the background; eggs are ellipses and backgrounds are not.

name: Threshold sweep proposals
why: No single level suits every image, so try many and let the ellipse test choose.

name: Add dark-side sweep
why: Against a white towel or bag the egg can be the darker region.

name: Relax ellipse test to 0.75
why: Fingers and shadows clip the outline, so 0.85 may reject true eggs. Many images currently return nothing.

name: Smoothness channel
why: Worst images are white eggs on white textured cloth, which brightness can't separate but texture can.

name: Whiteness + smoothness proposals
why: The channels fail on different images, so pool their proposals and let the selector pick.

name: Add pale and gray channels
why: More proposal sources for eggs that are neither bright nor on texture.

name: Felzenszwalb region proposals
why: Graph-based regions give closed object shapes where no threshold isolates the egg.

name: Stop filling holes, cap area at 0.45
why: Visual review of T13: background sheets with an egg-shaped hole, once filled, pass the ellipse test.

name: Edge-support selection on arcs
why: Regions split eggs along shading lines, yet the outline is visible nearly everywhere. Fit ellipses to Canny arcs, rank by how much perimeter sits on a normal gradient.

name: Penalise edges inside the ellipse
why: Ellipses fitted across textured background have support but a busy interior; a shell has a clean one.

name: Prefer larger ellipses
why: Small fits on a shading line can out-score the whole egg.

name: GrabCut boundary refinement
why: Eggs are not perfect ellipses and fingers occlude them; snap to real edges.

name: Penalise colour inside the ellipse
why: Review of T19: tubs and bowls are ellipses too, and T18's size bonus chose them. Shells are nearly colourless. Branches from T17, dropping the size bonus.

name: Lower support threshold to 1.5
why: White eggs on white surfaces have faint outlines that fall below 2.5 levels per pixel.

name: Lower Canny to (10, 30)
why: Faint outlines never become arcs, so no ellipse is even proposed.

name: Both lower thresholds
why: Combine T21 and T22.

name: 80 arcs instead of 40
why: Textured images produce many long arcs that crowd out the egg's.

name: Region proposals as extra ellipse seeds
why: T12's sweep found eggs on some images where arcs fail, so offer those as candidates too.

name: Back to threshold 2.5 with 80 arcs
why: T21 and T23 showed the 1.5 threshold does not help once Canny is lower, so drop it.

name: Keep ratio 0.75 to 0.9
why: Count accuracy is the weakest metric: extra ellipses score within 75% of the true egg.

name: Raise minimum score to 0.5
why: Absolute floor on weak single detections.

name: Polish ellipses onto edges
why: Boundary F1 is 0.57 with correct selections: arc fits are rough.

name: GrabCut in a narrow band
why: T19 GrabCut raised boundary F1, and selection is now right often enough to refine. Narrow band limits leaks.

name: GrabCut in a wide band
why: Compare with T30: does a wider band recover occlusions or just leak?

name: T24 thresholds, keep 0.9, wide GrabCut
why: T24 had the best IoU and T31 the best count and boundary. Combine them, without polish, which added cost for no gain.

name: Keep ratio 0.8
why: 0.9 costs recall on multi-egg images. Look for a middle ground.

name: Stronger interior penalty (4 to 8)
why: The interior penalty gave the largest single gain in T17, and foil and tubs still win sometimes.

name: Stronger colour penalty (1.5 to 2.5)
why: Same reasoning for colourful containers.

name: Lower bar for same-size eggs
why: Review of T32: 140 and 144 find 1 of 3 eggs. Eggs in a photo share a size and junk does not.

name: Penalise uneven brightness inside
why: Review of T32: bag-flap ellipses span a dark slit, an egg interior is even.

name: Same-size ratio 0.6
why: Check the sensitivity of the T36 value.

name: Gentler brightness penalty, lower floor
why: T37 failed because the penalty pushed true eggs below the fixed 0.35 floor, a flaw in the test. Retest fairly.

name: Same-size ratio 0.8
why: T36 at 0.7 traded too much precision. Try a milder bar.
